title: Chat stream router and ergonomic retry helpers for Python SDK
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: Customers building chat UIs want a single ergonomic surface for handling streaming tokens, structured events (tool calls / function calls), and lifecycle signals (done/error/cancel). Current Python SDK patterns are fragmented: some teams use async iterators, others callbacks; retry semantics are ad-hoc and don't integrate with streaming backpressure. Goal: implement a ChatStreamRouter and a small set of retry/backpressure helpers that make common patterns (UI streaming, server-side batching, streamed tool execution) straightforward while preserving low-level control when needed. Scope: API additions to the SDK only (no server-side changes). Deliverables: 1) ChatStreamRouter high-level API, 2) RetryPolicy helpers (exponential, idempotent-aware), 3) backpressure primitives (pause/resume/cancel) for async iterators, 4) two example apps (streaming chat UI and a server-side aggregator) and tests and docs.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce ChatStreamRouter class in sdk.chat.stream with documented public methods: attach(handler), detach(handler), start(request), stop(cancel_reason)
Provide an async-generator adapter: ChatStreamRouter.as_async_iter() that yields typed events (token, delta_update, function_call_start, function_call_chunk, done, error)

RetryPolicy helpers: RetryPolicy.exponential_backoff(), RetryPolicy.idempotent_only() and integration example showing automatic retries for transient network errors but not for server-side 4xx content errors
Backpressure controls: the async iterator returned supports .pause() and .resume() hooks; documented behavior with buffering limits and a TokenDropped metric when the UI can't keep up
Two runnable examples added under examples/python/streaming: ui_streaming_demo.py and aggregator_streaming_consumer.py with end-to-end unit/integration tests
API reviewed and approved by SDK lead and the Runtime team; PR merged and docs updated in the python SDK reference (docs/sdk/python/streams.md)
Performance: adding router/adapter should not add >5% median latency overhead in microbench against current streaming path (benchmark included)

notes: Design highlights and example snippets below for reviewers. These should be copied into the PR description as well. The patterns prioritize: explicit typed events for structured outputs, minimal surface area for new APIs, and clear boundaries for when retries are safe.
example_snippets:
# Example A - async iterator consumer (recommended for framework integrations)
async def stream_chat_example(client, prompt):
    router = client.chat.stream_router()
    async for evt in router.as_async_iter(prompt):
        if evt.type == 'token':
            ui.append_token(evt.text)
        elif evt.type == 'function_call_start':
            ui.show_spinner_for_function(evt.name)
        elif evt.type == 'function_call_chunk':
            function_stdout.write(evt.payload)
        elif evt.type == 'done':
            break
        elif evt.type == 'error':
            logger.error('stream error: %s', evt.message)

# consumer may call router.pause()/router.resume() to apply backpressure
# Example B - decorator event handlers for quick usage
router = client.chat.stream_router()
@router.on_event('token')
def on_token(evt):
    print(evt.text, end='')

@router.on_event('done')
def on_done(evt):
    print('
-- done --')

# start runs in background; returns a handle for cancellation
handle = router.start(prompt='Hello world')
# later
handle.cancel(reason='user_navigated_away')
# Example C - RetryPolicy usage
retry_policy = RetryPolicy.exponential_backoff(max_attempts=4, base_delay=0.25)
# attach to router.Start options so SDK will respect idempotency boundaries
router.start(prompt, retry_policy=retry_policy, idempotent_until='function_call_start')
# Backpressure notes:
# - router maintains an internal buffer of N events (default 64). When the consumer pauses, new incoming tokens will be buffered up to N. Beyond that, SDK emits a 'token_dropped' metric and will apply one of two strategies: drop-oldest or suspend reads from transport (configurable). For interactive UIs default = drop-oldest to avoid head-of-line latency.
# Metrics: token_received, token_emitted, token_dropped, stream_retries, stream_duration_seconds
